Exemplum 2.

§. 48. Sint applicatae, quae abscissis $n	heta$, $(1-n)	heta$, $(1+n)	heta$, $(2-n)	heta$, $(2+n)	heta$, etc. respondent:
$p=f$; $q=-f$; $r=+f$; $s=-f$; $t=+f$; $u=-f$; etc.
et per aequationem finitam inuestigetur relatio in genere inter abscissam $x=	heta\omega$ et applicatam $=y$.
Aequatio generalis §. 36. ad hunc casum accommodata praebet:
$ rac{2n\Delta y}{f(n-\omega)}= rac{1}{n-\omega}+ rac{1}{1-n-\omega}+ rac{1}{1+n-\omega}+ rac{1}{2-n-\omega}+ rac{1}{2+n-\omega}+	ext{etc.}$
$- rac{1}{n+\omega}- rac{1}{1-n+\omega}- rac{1}{1+n+\omega}- rac{1}{2-n+\omega}- rac{1}{2+n+\omega}-	ext{etc.}$
ubi nunc quidem nouimus esse
$\Delta= rac{(n-\omega)\pi\sin.2n\pi}{2n\sin.(n-\omega)\pi\sin.(n+\omega)\pi}$.
Illa autem series ex §. 39. fit
$	ext{I}-	ext{III}= rac{\pi}{	ang.(n-\omega)\pi}- rac{\pi}{	ang.(n+\omega)\pi}= rac{\pi\sin.2\omega\pi}{\sin.(n-\omega)\pi\cdot\sin.(n+\omega)\pi}$
qua summa substituta prodit

$y= rac{f\sin.2\omega\pi}{\sin.2n\pi}= rac{f\sin. rac{2x\pi}{	heta}}{\sin.2n\pi}$.

items.english: The stated ratio of integral formulas equals ν/(μ−ν) · sin((μ−ν)π/λ)/sin(νπ/λ), whose truth is shown from the following general theorem.

items.quote:
Sint applicatae, quae abscissis $n\theta$, $(1-n)\theta$, $(1+n)\theta$, $(2-n)\theta$, $(2+n)\theta$, etc. respondent:
$p=f$; $q=-f$; $r=+f$; $s=-f$; $t=+f$; $u=-f$; etc.
et per aequationem finitam inuestigetur relatio in genere inter abscissam $x=\theta\omega$ et applicatam $=y$.
items.english: Let the applicates corresponding to the abscissas nθ, (1−n)θ, (1+n)θ, (2−n)θ, (2+n)θ, etc. be p=f, q=−f, r=+f, s=−f, t=+f, u=−f, etc. Find, by a finite equation, the general relation between the abscissa x=θω and the applicate y.
